claims.notes: [BATCH NOTE b089] Batch-level scope decisions for this file (lines 157–274 only; lines 1–156 of the same document are batch b088 and were read for context but not extracted). Out of C4 scope per instrument rule 5 and therefore NOT extracted: changelog entry dates (2026-06-06/07/08), session numbers (Sessions 104–106), commit hashes (`bb7d5279`, `b0f0e199`), section cross-references (§1, §4b, §§3–4, §5), Obs identifiers (Obs 260), candidate identifiers (cand 2128), and numbers inside file/condition/config names (`55maps`, `pv-diag-384`, `consensus_t2.geojson`, `verified-v1-n5`, `t03_vs_t07_3of5`). Consensus-vote labels used purely to name a configuration in running prose (`3-of-5`, `4-of-5`, `5-of-5`, `2-of-5`, `T0.3`, `T0.7`, `vote=3 shells`, `vote=2`) are treated as condition names per rule 5, consistent with the `t0.3` example in the instrument; where a vote/temperature label is instead the subject of a numeric result the surrounding metric is extracted. Also treated as a descriptive label rather than a claim: 'the two-reference (Track 1 historical / Track 2 canonical) deliverable' (line 214). Anchor note for this claim: the GS 20 m buffer is anchored to the GS post-verifier temperature permutation, the only GS artefact in this run directory that records `buffer_metres` as a scalar; the ~25 m digitisation-jitter figure is asserted from Obs 260, which lives in prose (docs/notes/reflections/working-notes.md) — never anchored to prose per rule 2, so it is anchor-unknown for triage to chase.
